newsitem.title: JAPAN: DDI sees PHS units cutting losses in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: DDI sees PHS units cutting losses in 97/98.

text.p: Japanese telephone operator DDI Corp said on Thursday that it expects its nine personal handyphone (PHS) units to post a total net loss of ten billion yen in 1997/98, compared with an actual loss of 79.1 billion yen in the previous year.
The expected reduction in losses at the personal handyphone units this business year was a major factor behind an anticipated recovery in DDI's group net profit for the year.
DDI, which is about 22 percent owned by Kyocera Corp, forecast a group net profit of 29 billion yen in 1997/98 after suffering a loss of 26.16 billion yen in the previous year.

The company said in a statement that total net profits at its eight cellular phone units would rise about 35 percent year-on-year to 24 billion yen in 1997/98. In 1996/97, profits dropped about 38 percent to 17.8 billion yen.
DDI said that, on a parent basis, its capital spending would more than double to 124.3 billion yen in 1997/98 from the previous year's actual spending of 59.6 billion yen.

The eight cellular units plan a total of 170 billion yen in capital spending in 1997/98, down from 197.5 billion yen in the previous year, it said. The nine PHS units, meanwhile, plan capital spending of 80 billion yen this year, up modestly from the previous year's 76.8 billion yen, it added.

DDI's accumulated subscribers are expected to rise to 15.5 million by March 1998, while the cellular units' subscribers will rise to 4.5 million and the PHS units' subscribers to 4.2 million, DDI said.
At the end of March 1997, accumulated subscribers totalled 15 million at DDI itself, 3.42 million at its cellular units and 2.88 million at its PHS units, the company said.
